lines.t: Graveyard shift at K-LZQ,
Tiny town station, half past two.
DJ Danny with his coffee cold,
Spinnin’ soft rock, feelin’ old.
Clicks a file he’s never seen,
“Volumes Of Truth – Program 13.”
Shrugs and says, “What could go wrong?”
Then a thunder voice cuts through his song.
It said, “Awake, My people, the time is near,
You snooze in comfort, but the Trumpet’s clear.”
Danny froze with his donut bite,
Said, “Uh… folks, that wasn’t me tonight.”
Now the phones light up like a neon sign,
“Be caller one… caller two… now line.”
Every heart on the other end of the line
Gets shaken by a word that’s way too fine.
“Awake, My people, open your eyes,
Stop dreamin’ under darkened skies.”
DJ’s sweatin’ through his scripted line,
Waitin’ on the voice of caller number nine.
Caller three says, “Man, that hit deep,
Been driftin’ so long I fell asleep.”
Caller five says, “Who’s readin’ that?
It feels like God just crashed my chat.”
Danny taps keys, tries to fade it out,
But every button just reroutes.
The program jumps back, fills the air,
“Behold, the last trumpet, I’ve laid it bare.”
It said, “You cling to shadows, but I AM HE,
Turn from the dark, come back to Me.”
Danny whispers, “This ain’t in my log…”
Producer texts, “Just blame it on a fog.”
Now the phones light up like a neon sign,
Caller six, caller seven cross the line.
Every voice sayin’, “Something’s wrong,
But this strange broadcast feels so strong.”
“Awake, My people, your sleep must end,
Judgment is coming, but I still befriend.”
He reads the queue on the little screen,
Caller number nine’s marked: “Name unseen.”
Line nine crackles, voice real low,
“Hey DJ… I thought you should know.
Been runnin’ from God since ‘92,
But tonight those letters cut me through.
When it said, ‘Awake, the time has come,’
I heard my name in every drum.
I pulled my car to the shoulder side,
Been cryin’ here with the radio wide.”
Danny swallows, tosses out his script,
Says, “Friend, sounds like your heart just flipped.”
Caller nine laughs through a broken tone,
Says, “Feels like He read me on a microphone.”
Now the board lights fade but the truth stays bright,
Dead air filled with a living light.
No more games, no canned line,
Just a DJ prayin’ with caller nine.
“Awake, My people,” the playback said,
“Turn from the brink, come home instead.”
Danny kills the ads, lets silence ring,
Says, “If you’re still listenin’, this is your ding.”
Morning crew walks in at six-oh-four,
Finds Danny teary on the studio floor.
Says, “We don’t know where that file came from,
But half the town just beat the drum.”
They rename the slot, that graveyard time,
“The Volumes Hour – Wake-Up Line.”
And every night ‘round 2:09,
He listens close… for caller number nine.
